institution_or_resource: Weigel–Tyroff Verlagskupfer chain: Ethica Naturalis ca.1700 → Huy und Pfuy 1707 → Die Grösse und Mannigfaltigkeit 1766
reported_scope: Primary 1766 preface states old coppers were already in the publisher's office, previously used, uneconomic to replace, and calls them Verlagskupfer. Met/DNB/DDB/Folger controls resolve Ethica publisher as elder Christoph Weigel (1654–1725) with Jan/Caspar Luyken as designers/printmakers. LEO-BW/HAB records Huy und Pfuy 1707 with 100 copperplates and Christoph Weigel as publisher. A surviving-copy description tied to VD18 14823888-001 styles the 1766 publisher 'J. D. Tyroff der ältern Christoph Weigels seel. Erb.'; Rijksmuseum independently catalogues J.D. Tyroff 1766 and says the Luyken engravings first appeared in Ethica Naturalis ca.1700.
relevance: Direct actor-level evidence that reusable publisher-held copper stock could outlive textual hosts and the original publisher, pass through Weigel/Tyroff succession, and receive new textual/didactic programmes
